observation: A meta-analysis of 38 studies found moderate-magnitude between-group effects for both phonological and visuospatial working memory in adults with ADHD vs controls.
claim: Adult ADHD working-memory deficits are real and moderate in size, so Riemann should not assume a constant working-memory budget for Sam.

implications.text: Keep element interactivity per screen/level low, since Sam's working-memory ceiling is on average lower than a neurotypical baseline the general cognitive-load literature assumes.

observation: Kofler et al. 2013 (319-study meta-analysis, fact-checked and confirmed) found reaction-time variability (RTV) is elevated in ADHD (children g~0.76, adults g~0.46); once RTV is accounted for, ADHD groups do not show slower mean processing speed -- variability, not average speed, is the signature. Stimulant medication reduced RTV (g~-0.74).
claim: Sam's attentional capacity spikes and craters unpredictably within a session rather than being uniformly reduced -- Riemann should design for a fluctuating, not a constantly-low, attention budget.
mechanism: Intra-individual reaction-time variability reflects moment-to-moment lapses in sustained attentional control, distinct from a fixed processing-speed deficit.
population: adults and children with ADHD (319-study meta-analysis)
context: large meta-analysis, replicated across age groups

implications.text: Let the user re-enter a document at any abstraction level at any time without penalty or forced restart-from-L0, since the moment they can engage is unpredictable, not schedulable.

observation: The dual-pathway model proposes ADHD arises via two largely independent routes: executive/cognitive dysregulation and motivational dysregulation (delay aversion, altered reward-delay signalling via dopaminergic frontoventral-striatal circuits).
claim: The subjective cost of waiting is itself aversive for Sam, independent of executive function -- anything that defers gratification (e.g. a long read before any payoff) taxes him more than word count alone suggests.
mechanism: Delay itself is processed as an aversive/costly state via altered reward-delay signalling, separate from any executive/working-memory limitation.
context: influential theoretical model with converging behavioural/neuroimaging support

implications.text: Make the L0 gist render near-instantly (sub-second perceived latency) so the wait cost of opening even a large document is close to zero -- an anti-avoidance mechanism, not just a convenience.

observation: Dodson's 'interest-based nervous system' (PINCH: passion, interest, novelty, challenge/competition) is widely repeated in ADHD media but has no peer-reviewed operationalization or controlled test of the construct itself.
claim: Interest/novelty/challenge framing is a plausible practitioner design heuristic for engaging Sam, but should not be presented as established science.

implications.text: Weight novelty/interest cues in surfacing/notification design as a soft heuristic (e.g. novel content gets slightly more prominent surfacing) but not as a validated mechanism to over-rely on.

observation: A meta-analysis of 20 resting-state studies found reduced core-DMN connectivity but elevated dorsomedial-prefrontal-subsystem connectivity in ADHD; a separate adolescent study tied DMN connectivity to delay aversion/temporal discounting specifically, not directly to mind-wandering.
claim: The popular 'DMN doesn't switch off in ADHD, causing mind-wandering' narrative is not what the more careful evidence shows; any Riemann design rationale citing DMN-causes-distraction should be softened or dropped.
context: meta-analytic connectivity findings plus one adolescent study; causal link to mind-wandering contested

implications.text: Avoid citing 'DMN intrusion causes mind-wandering' as design rationale anywhere in Riemann's documentation or copy; the better-supported link is DMN connectivity to delay aversion, already covered by F03-03.

observation: Barkley frames ADHD as fundamentally a disorder of time perception/self-regulation; hyperfocus and time blindness are described as the same underlying time-perception deficit expressed in opposite directions.
claim: Sam is likely to systematically misjudge how long a read will take and how long he has spent reading, in both directions (underestimating a long read, losing track of time inside an absorbing one).
context: clinical-practice writing plus converging behavioural time-estimation evidence

implications.text: Show a live elapsed/remaining read-time estimate as the user scrolls or the dial moves, directly countering time blindness during a reading session.

observation: Controlled studies (Montali & Lewandowski 1996; Rogowsky et al. 2016; Valentini et al.) show less-skilled readers' comprehension in a bimodal (simultaneous text+audio) condition matches average readers' visual-only comprehension, and bimodal presentation aids vocabulary acquisition; CLT researchers separately flag a redundancy-effect risk for skilled readers.
claim: Simultaneous, word/sentence-synced text+audio meaningfully helps weaker or fatigued readers, but the benefit is contested for skilled readers where it risks adding extraneous redundant load.
mechanism: Bimodal input offloads part of the decoding burden to the auditory channel for readers whose visual decoding is effortful, at the cost of some redundant-channel processing for readers who don't need that offload.
population: less-skilled and average readers (mixed ages, not ADHD-specific)

implications.text: Offer synced text+audio with word/sentence-level highlight-as-you-listen at L2/L3 (not just a plain read-aloud toggle), prioritized for longer/denser levels where reading alone is more taxing.

observation: An EEG-based study found bionic font offered no measurable benefit to ADHD readers; a separate 2022 controlled study found no significant speed/comprehension improvement for bionic vs normal text in general readers.
claim: Bionic-reading-style bolded-prefix rendering has no credible evidence of benefit for ADHD readers and should not be built as a serious feature.
population: adults with ADHD (EEG study) and general readers (2022 controlled study)
context: one EEG lab study, one controlled behavioural study

implications.text: Do not build bionic-reading bolded-prefix rendering as a core feature; if included at all, label it explicitly as unproven and opt-in only, and spend the engineering budget on bimodal audio sync instead.

observation: Soderlund et al. 2007 proposed stochastic resonance for white noise boosting ADHD memory-task performance; a 2024 study found inattentive-predominant profiles benefit from noise while hyperactive/impulsive-predominant profiles perform worse under the same noise, with roughly a third of participants harmed.
claim: A uniform 'add background white noise' focus feature would help a majority but measurably hurt a meaningful minority of ADHD users, and should never be a silent default.
mechanism: Proposed as stochastic resonance/moderate-brain-arousal: noise boosts a weak neural signal for under-aroused (inattentive) profiles but adds unwanted stimulation for already-overaroused (hyperactive/impulsive) profiles.
population: children and adults with ADHD, split by inattentive vs hyperactive/impulsive subtype
context: lab studies; subtype-reversal finding is newer/single-study, mechanism contested

implications.text: Make any ambient/white-noise focus feature opt-in and per-session togglable, and let the user's own dwell/reversal data determine whether it helps them, rather than assuming population-level benefit.

observation: Multiple studies (via UC Davis and CHADD summaries) find adults with ADHD perform better on cognitive tasks when allowed to fidget, with fidgeting increasing as time-on-task/attention wanes, consistent with a self-regulatory arousal function rather than mere boredom.
claim: Physical restlessness/fidgeting during a reading session should not be treated as a failure state or auto-paused; movement-tolerant interaction is more evidence-aligned than a rigid focus-lock UI.
mechanism: Fidgeting appears to self-regulate flagging arousal/alertness as sustained attention wanes over a task.
context: multiple converging peer-reviewed studies via reputable secondary summaries

implications.text: Do not build any 'hold still' or strict focus-lock UI chrome; do not penalize scrolling/dial-jiggling or auto-pause on small mouse movements.

observation: W3C COGA's 'Making Content Usable' guide (living draft, disability-general not ADHD-specific) recommends: short content chunks with generous white space, plain short sentences, clear headings/boundaries/regions, consistent familiar navigation, minimized memory demands (no forced re-entry of info), help accessible from anywhere in a task, and personalization support.
claim: Riemann's page chrome should follow COGA patterns directly: short chunks, plain short sentences at L0/L1, consistent navigation across sessions, an always-available help/get-unstuck affordance, and an explicit way to turn off animation/distraction.
population: people with cognitive and learning disabilities (disability-general, includes ADHD-adjacent guidance)
context: maintained multi-stakeholder accessibility standard, not a single experimental result

implications.text: Keep dial position and page controls in a consistent, familiar location across sessions (stable navigation), and never force re-entry of already-given information.
Provide an always-available 'help/get unstuck' affordance from anywhere in a reading session.
Provide an explicit control to turn off any animation/distraction.

observation: Searches for chunking/bullet-point-specific research turned up almost entirely UX-blog/marketing content restating general Cognitive Load Theory, without controlled comprehension studies specific to bullets vs prose.
claim: The general claim 'bullet points reduce cognitive load' is weakly evidenced (marketing-tier), distinct from and weaker than COGA's disability-specific chunking guidance (F03-11), which should be preferred as the citation for chunking decisions.

implications.text: Cite COGA (F03-11), not generic 'bullets reduce load' claims, as the basis for chunking/formatting decisions in design documentation.

observation: An 8-week RCT of a gamified educational application in children with ADHD found greater improvement than controls in visual/auditory reaction time, sustained attention, and reading/writing/math scores.
claim: Gamification/immediate feedback has real RCT-level benefit for ADHD attention and academic performance in children, but this is a pediatric, learning-task result that should not be directly extrapolated to an adult engineering student's summarization-tool reading use case.

implications.text: Prefer making every dial movement and level-change feel instantly, visibly responsive (smooth transitions, live word-count/read-time updates) over adding points/streaks or gamification-for-its-own-sake, which risks feeling patronizing to an adult and isn't evidenced for this population/use case.

observation: A literature-coverage scan of HCI venues (CHI, ASSETS, arXiv) found active ADHD-specific interaction research on video-watching customization, VR body-doubling, and neurodivergent learning states, but comparatively little on text-abstraction/summarization UIs specifically.
claim: A zoom-dial abstraction-tree interface for ADHD readers is comparatively under-studied territory in ADHD HCI research relative to video and co-presence tools.

implications.text: Treat Riemann's zoom-dial-for-ADHD-readers concept as a genuinely novel research contribution rather than assuming prior HCI work has already validated this specific pattern; build in-product evaluation rather than relying on transfer from adjacent ADHD-HCI work.

observation: Tiimo (2025 Apple App of the Year) replaces text to-do lists with colour-coded visual timelines/countdown timers addressing time blindness; Goblin.tools uses AI to break a single task into micro-steps addressing task-initiation friction; reviewers note Tiimo is strong on 'when' but weak on 'how to start' if a task feels overwhelming.
claim: Making time visible (elapsed/remaining) and lowering the activation cost of starting are two separable, both-valuable interventions for ADHD users, validated in the market though not by controlled studies.
context: product reviews and marketing-adjacent commentary, not controlled studies

implications.text: Build a cheap, word-count-based live read-time estimate (time-made-visible) as a distinct feature from lowering the activation energy of opening a document (the L0-gist-as-preview pattern, F03-17).

observation: Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria (RSD) is a widely used clinical-practice (not DSM-5, not formally diagnostic) term for intense shame/rejection reactions linked speculatively to dopamine deficits, driving avoidance-based perfectionism and task paralysis.
claim: RSD is a real, clinically-observed phenomenon useful as design intuition but should never be presented to Sam or in Riemann documentation as an established diagnostic construct.
mechanism: Speculatively proposed as dopamine-deficiency-driven emotional flooding triggered by perceived criticism or falling short.

implications.text: Design any shame-adjacent UI states (e.g. incomplete-reading indicators, streak resets) with explicit neutrality, since shame/avoidance around imperfection is a documented ADHD-relevant risk.

observation: Mahan's 'Wall of Awful' coaching metaphor describes accumulated negative-association 'bricks' around a task category (each past bad experience) that raise the activation cost of starting, disproportionate to actual task difficulty; commonly cited examples include email, multi-step projects, reading, and writing.
claim: The felt difficulty of starting with a raw document is disproportionate to its true complexity for Sam; the abstraction tree's real value may be less 'compression for speed' and more 'a zero-accumulated-bad-association entry point.'
mechanism: Repeated past friction/failure with a task category accumulates as an emotional barrier to starting that is independent of the current task's actual difficulty.
context: ADHD coaching practice, no controlled measurement

implications.text: Frame L0 explicitly as a low-stakes preview, not a commitment to read the whole document, to bypass Wall-of-Awful task-initiation friction.

observation: A 2026 arXiv paper on VR body doubling for ADHD explicitly states controlled studies have yet to show conclusive effects and mechanisms remain unclear; its own pilot (n=12) found faster task completion and perceived accuracy/attention with a human or AI body double vs. working alone.
claim: Body doubling is popular in ADHD communities but has almost no controlled evidence; a body-doubling-style feature (e.g. an AI presence during reading) would be an unvalidated bet, not an evidence-backed one.
context: single small pilot study, popular but under-researched practice

implications.text: Do not prioritize a body-doubling/co-presence feature on the strength of current evidence; flag as unvalidated if considered.

observation: Short-acting stimulants have onset 30-45 min and wear off in 3-6 hours; long-acting/extended-release formulations give symptom control 8-12 hours, with lisdexamfetamine showing efficacy out to ~14 hours; RTV specifically is reduced by stimulants (g~-0.74) but not by non-stimulant treatment; one source states stimulants improve attention/concentration but do not reliably improve learning/academic achievement in adult college students with ADHD.
claim: Sam's cognitive state varies in large, time-bounded, individual, and non-observable-from-interaction-alone ways across a day due to medication pharmacokinetics -- this argues for a manual, cheap 'how much capacity do I have right now' input rather than trying to infer state from behaviour alone.
mechanism: Stimulant medication alters the attentional substrate (via time-bounded pharmacokinetic windows) without necessarily changing comprehension/retention outcomes on its own.
context: well-established prescribing pharmacokinetics; academic-learning claim more contested

implications.text: Provide a cheap, explicit, manual state-check-in control ('how much capacity right now') rather than attempting to infer medication/energy state purely from interaction signals.
